html:
The surrender of Trebizond on the Black Sea coast of Anatolia to the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II on 15 August 1461. It ended the Empire of Trebizond, the last Greek state that claimed the Byzantine inheritance.

The empire had been founded in 1204 by the Komnenos family as Constantinople fell to the Fourth Crusade. It survived for two and a half centuries on trade and clever marriages. After the fall of Constantinople in 1453, and the Ottoman conquest of the Morea in 1460, it stood alone.

Its emperor David had counted on allies, above all Uzun Hasan of the Aq Qoyunlu Turkmen. Mehmed marched by land while his fleet blockaded the city, and the allies did not come. David gave up the city after a short siege on a promise of safety. He lived in exile until 1463, when Mehmed had him and most of his family executed.
